requirement.original: CronList tool inline conversation card is too verbose (full INPUT/OUTPUT blocks). Simplify inline card to Bash/subagent pattern: header+icon + one compact summary line of the input arguments only. Move the existing verbose INPUT+OUTPUT rendering to the right-side sidebar detail panel only. This establishes the general rule for all tool cards. This is spec §5.18.
requirement.clarified: Register CronList in knownTools.tsx with minimal:true so the inline card shows only the compact header row. The sidebar already uses SidebarGenericView as its fallback for unregistered tools, which correctly renders full INPUT+OUTPUT — no sidebar changes needed.
requirement.what: Add CronList to knownTools.tsx with minimal:true + icon + extractDescription; add i18n keys to all 9 language files
requirement.why: CronList currently falls through to ToolView's default ToolContent renderer which renders full INPUT+OUTPUT blocks inline in the conversation, making the card too verbose. The compact-inline pattern is established by BashView/SidebarBashView.

root_cause_analysis.symptom: CronList tool call card renders full INPUT + OUTPUT code blocks inline in the conversation
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: CronList is not registered in knownTools.tsx. ToolView.tsx resolves knownTool as undefined for CronList, so minimal defaults to false (via resolveFlags: isMcp=false, knownTool=undefined, minimal stays false). With minimal=false, ToolContent renders at ToolView.tsx:129 showing the default INPUT/OUTPUT layout.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A — CronList was never registered; this is a missing registration, not a regression
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: CronList is a Claude Code built-in tool that was never added to the happy-app tool registry when the registry was created
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: Without a registry entry, CronList falls through to the generic verbose renderer which shows full JSON INPUT + OUTPUT inline, violating the compact-inline design pattern
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Pre-existing gap from when the tool registry was first established
